references.text: God tells Moses that no one can see his face and live, which reflects Manoah's fear of dying after seeing God.
Jacob names the place Peniel because he saw God face to face and yet his life was spared, the same theme as in Manoah's statement.
The Lord warns Moses that the people must not break through to see the Lord, or many of them will die.
The Israelites express fear of dying after hearing God's voice and seeing his glory, the same fear that Manoah expresses.
Gideon fears he will die because he has seen the angel of the Lord face to face, but the Lord assures him that he will not die.
Isaiah cries out that he is doomed because he has seen the King, the Lord of hosts, with his own eyes.
